risk_note: RV2, payout + risk, no migration, no contract change, no money moves (withdraw lane, model Claude Fable 5.1; orchestrator rulings D10-537 ③, D10-681, D10-687). 08 BR-ID-36 requires a risk_hits row for every rule hit; the withdrawal side wrote none. (1) Submission: a POST /v1/withdrawals refused by the blocklist (44001, BR-WDR-03 ③a, BR-ID-31) now records one blocked_request hit (request_type withdraw, member, applied amount in whole fen, the account's current phone as digest + masked number, dimension / value digest / rule code). The 44001 answer is unchanged and still not stored with the idempotency key; the application's transaction rolls back as before and the hit is written afterwards by risk's blocklist service in its own short transaction (the bind-phone precedent), only for a 44001 the handler produced in this call, without a second rule-status read. A failed record answers 5xx; nothing is created, debited or cached either way. (2) Automatic payout: the live BR-WDR-29 ⑨ check is still made once; when the decision lists risk_flag:blacklist_hit one hit (ref_type withdrawal, risk_action manual_review) is written on the decision's transaction, so it commits or rolls back with the decision and a withdrawal has at most one. BlocklistMatchReader.read() and AutoPayoutBlacklistReader.hit() keep their shapes (frozen [AC-B2-11f#1/#2/#4/#6/#7], [AC-B2-05c#67]); the target comes from new optional match() members. Real risks: a hit recorded without a decision or twice (covered: same key twice gives two refusals and two hits by rule; idempotency-layer answers record nothing; redelivery and concurrent decisions give one), and a wrong related phone (money r1 S1, fixed: digest and masked number are read on one REPEATABLE READ snapshot). An account without a phone never reaches ③a (identity stage ⑧ answers 10005 first); the writer still stores both related phone columns as null for it. Test-machine full verify not run (AWS runners disabled, D10-555; CI verify-int is the full verification, approvals 21); the red run and the implementation's run of the task's rule tests were made in the local Docker container.

reviews.note: Codex via codex-run.sh, static, read-only; three calls, the limit. r1 (base = spec round 2, implementation 067879712) failed on one S1: the recorder read users.phone_hmac and the masked number in two statements, so a phone change committed between them could pair the old digest with the new masked number (BR-ID-36: the related phone is the account's current one). Fixed by reading both on one REPEATABLE READ, read-only transaction that ends before the hit is written. r2: its answer was a pass, but validate-output rejected the output (exit 10, counted, no usable output) because the lane passed --base = the round-3 spec commit while the checklist cited the two round-3 test files, which are outside that base..HEAD diff; a dispatch mistake of the lane, reported to the orchestrator, the rejected file is not evidence. r3 (base = the fork point 563c5b91091a, the whole task diff; codex-run's incremental chain names it round 2) passed: S1 closed, no findings, checklist rounding ok, sign n/a, idempotency ok, concurrency ok, partial_refund n/a, clock ok, app_id ok. Reviewed at 7b98871e6 before the landing rebase; the implementation commits are unchanged by it.

spec_test_review.note: Codex wrote the rule tests in 3 attempts, the limit (test/spec/payout/withdraw-blocklist-hits: submit, match, auto, review-writer, digest-writer and two kits; 39 tests).
